Given:
- Length of line $AB = 50\text{ mm}$
- End A is $30\text{ mm}$ above H.P. and $20\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P.
- Front view of the line is a point.

### **Analysis:**
Since the front view of line $AB$ is a point, the line must be **perpendicular to the V.P.** (and parallel to the H.P.). This means both ends $A$ and $B$ lie on the same projector perpendicular to V.P.
- Length of the line is $50\text{ mm}$, and it is perpendicular to V.P., hence it is parallel to H.P.
- Top view will show the true length ($50\text{ mm}$) perpendicular to the $XY$ line.

### **Drawing Steps:**
1. Draw a reference line $XY$.
2. Locate the front view point $a'b'$ at $30\text{ mm}$ above the $XY$ line.
3. Draw a projector line downwards from $a'b'$.
4. From the projector line on the $XY$ line, measure $20\text{ mm}$ downwards to locate top view of end A ($a$).
5. Since the length is $50\text{ mm}$, measure $50\text{ mm}$ downwards from point $a$ along the projector to locate top view of end B ($b$).
6. The top view is a line segment $ab$ of length $50\text{ mm}$ perpendicular to $XY$.
proTip: A line perpendicular to V.P. has its front view as a point and top view showing true length perpendicular to XY.
